title: Two fates for a seed
hook: An animal can move a seed or destroy it.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: In this toy example, one seed is carried and dropped intact elsewhere; another is eaten and destroyed. Which seed was dispersed intact?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: In this toy example, one seed is carried and dropped intact elsewhere; another is eaten and destroyed. Which seed was dispersed intact?

claims.text: In this toy example, one seed is carried and dropped intact elsewhere; another is eaten and destroyed. Which seed was dispersed intact? The bird carries one stipulated seed and drops it intact at a new location; the other seed is eaten and destroyed. Seed dispersal and seed predation have different consequences for that seed. An intact dropped seed is not guaranteed to germinate.
claims.source: Stipulated illustrative scenario, not wildlife observations. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
An animal carries a seed away and drops it intact. What has happened to that seed? The stipulated seed was carried to a different location, while germination is not guaranteed.
